newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain sees growth picking up in H2 1996.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain sees growth picking up in H2 1996.

text.p: The Bank of Spain said on Friday that it expects economic growth to have picked up in the second half of 1996.
In its twice yearly inflation report, the central bank also said it sees "considerable scope" for further reduction in inflation.
It also reiterated a call for wage moderation and structural reform.
But a rise in growth hinged on a revival in the German economy, the central bank said.

Gross domestic product growth in the second quarter showed an acceleration over previous quarters, which "means we can predict higher rates of expansion as the second half progresses," the report said.

The Bank of Spain noted progress had already been made in reducing inflation. But the report added "despite the progress achieved, the scope that separates us from the reference point (the three percent Bank of Spain target for 1997) is still considerable and the path isn't free of difficulties."
The Bank of Spain also said it considered "high" the difference between Spanish inflation and that of the average of the three most stable nations in the European Union.
The report warned of the inflationary risks tied to the development of unit labour costs.
The Bank of Spain said that "wages should adjust to the overall pace of convergence and the inflation rates of the most stable EU countries."
It also advised that "continued wage moderation be accompanied by structural changes aimed at improving the way the economy works."
The central bank recommended rigorous control of public spending.
The report, written before the presentation to parliament earlier this week of the 1997 budget draft, praised the budget for allowing Spain to narrow its public deficit to three percent of GDP.

"The direction of budget policy creates favourable conditions for macroeconomic stability and financial market confidence, and allows monetary policy to perform its task of meeting inflation targets," the report said.
